- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥1.0) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion.
- When sentiment is negative (≤-1.0) or mixed, model often underestimates or lags behind true price movements; increase forecast slightly to capture momentum.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior day), model frequently overshoots in the next 3–5 days; apply a downward correction of 2–5% to prevent overreaction.
- If true price deviates significantly from 30-day moving average (e.g., >±3%), model often fails to revert; apply a mean-reversion adjustment toward prior 10–15 day average.
- For forecasts with high volatility in sentiment history (alternating +/–), model tends to overfit short-term noise; smooth forecasts using 5-day weighted average to reduce false signals.
- If sentiment turns negative after a positive streak, model often fails to adjust quickly; reduce forecast by 1–3% per day of negative sentiment buildup.
